documents.title: Progress in anticancer chemical constituents and pharmacological research of Carpesium cernuum L. (Review).
documents.abstract: The present study aimed to systematically review the anticancer chemical constituents, pharmacological effects, and molecular targets of Carpesium cernuum L., clarify the molecular network of its anticancer mechanisms, summarize the research achievements and limitations and provide a scientific reference for its development and utilization, the research and development of novel anticancer drugs, and clinical applications. Through literature collation and experimental data integration, the chemical constituents of C. cernuum were classified and identified, and with the aid of in vitro cell expe

documents.title: Lessons From CABBI: Advancing Vegetative Oil Production in C4 Crops Through a Vertically Integrated DBTL Framework.
documents.abstract: The global demand for renewable liquid fuels and biobased chemicals has intensified interest in engineering high-biomass C4 grasses to accumulate triacylglycerol (TAG) in vegetative tissues. Achieving this goal requires coordinated solutions across molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment, disciplines that rarely operate within a single research program. The Center for Advanced Bioenergy and Bioproducts Innovation (CABBI) was established to provide this integration through a Design-Build-Test-Learn (DBTL) framework applied to three C4 feedstocks: sacchar

documents.title: Impact of EEG-related HPO terms on phenotype-driven variant prioritization in pediatric epilepsy.
documents.abstract: The Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) is a standardized resource of hierarchically organized phenotypic terms used for deep phenotyping, both in research and diagnosis. In our study, we aimed to investigate how the specificity of EEG-related HPO terms may impact phenotype and gene scoring and prioritization.

documents.title: LACA: a cross-species single-cell resource for exploring longevity and aging-associated cellular and molecular programs.
documents.abstract: Different species can have various maximum lifespans, some with exceptional longevity, yet the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Despite rapid advances in single-cell transcriptomics, resources that systematically connect single-cell gene expression profiles to species lifespan are limited. We hereby present the Longevity & Aging Cell Atlas (LACA), a database that integrates single-cell transcriptomic datasets across 134 species with their maximum lifespans. LACA includes over 148 million cells with 190 annotated cell types from single-cell datasets. LACA a

documents.title: PRGdb 5.0: a multi-layered resource for plant resistance gene discovery and exploration.
documents.abstract: Plant Resistance Genes database (PRGdb) 5.0 (https://prgdb.org/prgdb5/) is a major update of the PRGdb, designed to expand plant disease resistance gene resources within a unified web platform. The release incorporates predictions for 97 plant proteomes and adds 288, 315 new putative resistance-associated proteins, bringing the database to 874,967 candidate resistance proteins from 279 plant proteomes. The curated reference collection increased from 199 to 462 experimentally supported resistance proteins. To complement domain-based classification, the platform introduces an AI-assisted priorit

documents.title: The mOTUs-db in 2027: linking taxonomy, genome-encoded function, and biogeography across environments.
documents.abstract: A molecular understanding of microbial communities requires linking taxonomic composition to the genome-resolved functional potential of member taxa. However, this integration remains challenging since representative genomes from cultivated strains are unavailable. Here, we present a new release of the mOTUs database, which extends genome coverage of underexplored environments and enriches its 3.9 million genome collection with functional annotations. Samples are annotated with a new hierarchical environmental ontology and geographic coordinates, supporting customizable sample grouping and bio

documents.title: A multi-layer, multi-species graph-based framework for comparative analysis of sRNA-mediated regulation.
documents.abstract: Small RNAs (sRNAs) are central post-transcriptional regulators of bacterial gene expression, yet their evolutionary dynamics remain difficult to resolve due to limited sequence conservation. While sequence-homologous sRNAs can retain or diverge in function, unrelated sRNAs may independently evolve to regulate similar biological processes, making functional conservation invisible to sequence-based approaches. Here, we present a multi-layer, multi-species graph-based framework that integrates experimentally detected sRNA-messenger RNA interactions, orthology relationships, functional annotations

documents.title: CellStressDB: an AI-powered database of cellular responses to physical stressors.
documents.abstract: Physical stressors profoundly influence cellular behavior by triggering coordinated stress-response programs that regulate signaling, gene expression, metabolism, and cell fate. Here, we present CellStressDB (https://cellstressdb.omic.tech), an AI-powered database for exploring cellular responses to physical stressors. The current release contains data from 131 transcriptomic studies, with 2 364 816 cell and 1205 bulk sample observations from human and mouse across nine physical-stress classes and 21 tissue categories. Data and analyses are organized into 2848 indexed analysis entries across 7

documents.title: A Graded Immune-Cell-Resolved cis-eQTL Mendelian Randomisation Screen Across Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Related Immune Phenotypes.
documents.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a genetically complex autoimmune disease. Whole-blood expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) analyses capture average regulatory effects across leukocytes, whereas SLE involves immune processes that depend on cell context. Therefore, a cell-resolved screen requires rigorous verification of instrument identity, allele orientation, and the multiple-testing denominator before biological interpretation.

documents.title: PDBe in 2027: integrating literature annotations, molecular dynamics data, and AI-ready access.
documents.abstract: The Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe; pdbe.org) provides open access to experimentally determined biomacromolecular structures and enriches these data with biological and functional context. Here, we describe recent developments that expand the information connected to PDB structures and introduce new ways for researchers and computational tools to access it. Literature integration has been extended to additional open-access publications, substantially increasing the availability of residue-level annotations mined from the scientific literature. Cross-links to molecular dynamics simulations i

documents.title: ONITH: An ontology-based non-clinical integration and term harmonization pipeline for data reuse in 3R.
documents.abstract: Animal studies continue to play a critical role in drug development as they uniquely capture the physiological complexity required to elucidate drug mechanisms and safety profiles. However, in alignment with the 3R principles (Reduce, Refine, Replace), there is a growing ethical and regulatory commitment to minimizing animal use. As part of this effort, the reuse of existing data has emerged as a potential strategy to support the transition toward more data-driven approaches in drug development, a direction that is increasingly supported by regulatory authorities as a viable alternative to ani
documents.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine

documents.title: Multi-omics-constrained kinetic models quantify pathway rewiring and predict metabolic vulnerabilities in BRCA1-deficient ovarian cancer.
documents.abstract: Time-resolved, network-wide consequences of cancer metabolic reprogramming remain poorly understood. We built multi-omics-constrained, near-genome-scale kinetic ensembles for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells. Covering over 2,100 reactions, the ensembles enabled uncertainty-quantified simulations of nutrient, metabolite, and enzyme perturbations. Metabolic control analysis identified 28 enzyme-mediated vulnerabilities; 24 are linked to experimental or approved DrugBank compounds, whereas four lack documented drug associations. Independent DepMap data supported a su

documents.title: PANTHER: the protein tree and function resource in 2027.
documents.abstract: PANTHER (Protein ANalysis THrough Evolutionary Relationships) is a comprehensive resource of phylogenetic trees of protein-coding gene families. Trees are manually annotated with Gene Ontology (GO) terms describing how protein functional characteristics were gained and lost over time along tree branches, and these evolutionary models are used to create GO annotations for protein-coding genes. Orthologs, paralogs, and xenologs are assigned based on the trees. Here, we describe updates to the PANTHER resource since our previous published report in 2022. Since that time, the content of the databa

documents.title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.
documents.abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of ge

documents.title: gcPathogen 2.0: an expanded multi-omics database advancing global pathogen surveillance and One Health research.
documents.abstract: Launched in 2024, gcPathogen established a critical foundation for the genomic surveillance of human pathogens. Here, we present gcPathogen 2.0, a major multi-omics update designed to address key analytical bottlenecks, including the integration of genomic and transcriptional profiles, systematic tracking of cross-habitat distribution, and large-scale discovery of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). This release expands coverage from 1134 to 1506 pathogenic species, spanning 557 bacteria, 508 fungi, 258 viruses, and 183 parasites, and increases total genomic records past 2.3 million. By incorporati

documents.title: Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC): an integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform.
documents.abstract: The rapid growth of metabolomics data has increased the need for integrated storage, analysis, and reuse. Here, we present Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC) V1.0 (https://metabolomics.dicp.ac.cn/), an integrated database and platform for standardized data deposition, spectral-resource management, online analysis, and disease-focused knowledge mining. The deposition framework captures project, sample, pretreatment, and instrument metadata across chromatographic, capillary electrophoresis-mass spectrometry, and nuclear magnetic resonance workflows. Met-SC contains 7  756  867 reference spectra ass

documents.title: Conversational Multi-Agentic Network-Driven Disease Module Identification and Drug Repurposing Prediction With ChatDRex: Platform Development Study.
documents.abstract: Repurposing approved drugs offers a time- and cost-effective alternative to traditional drug development. However, in silico prediction of repurposing candidates is challenging and requires the effective collaboration of specialists in various fields, including pharmacology, medicine, biology, and bioinformatics. Fragmented, specialized algorithms and tools often address only narrow aspects of the overall problem. Heterogeneous, unstructured data landscapes require the expertise of specialized users. Hence, diverse data sources might not integrate smoothly across workflows.

documents.title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.
documents.abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe),

documents.title: Integration of single-cell multi-omic data with graph-based topic modelling.
documents.abstract: Recent advances in single-cell biology enable the profiling of multiple molecular layers, such as the transcriptome, epigenome, and surface proteins, within a single cell. Tackling the complexity of these data from multiple perspectives allows researchers to gain the most comprehensive insights into cellular biological properties. Here, we propose a graph-based topic modelling method called bionSBM. Our method leverages well-known community-detection methods for multipartite graphs and the interpretability of topic modelling to cluster and explain high-dimensional, sparse, and noisy single-cel

documents.title: Functional Analysis of GarCIPK8 from Gossypium aridum Conferring Salt Stress Tolerance in Gossypium hirsutum.
documents.abstract: Soil salinization is a major abiotic stress factor restricting global agricultural production. The CBL-CIPK signaling network, comprising calcineurin B-like proteins (CBLs) and CBL-interacting protein kinases (CIPKs), plays a critical role in plant adaptation to salt stress. Here, we focused on GarCIPK8, a CIPK gene previously isolated from the diploid wild cotton Gossypium aridum, and generated its overexpressing transgenic lines in G. hirsutum through Agrobacterium-mediated transformation. Under 300 mmol/L NaCl treatment, transgenic plants showed markedly enhanced growth performance, with gr

documents.title: Crystalline silica particles exposure modulated miRNA expression profiles in human macrophage-like THP-1 cells.
documents.abstract: Occupational and environmental exposure to crystalline silica particles is a major global health concern linked to silicosis, pulmonary fibrosis, autoimmune disease, and lung cancer. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate gene expression post-transcriptionally and are emerging as potential effect biomarkers of exposure in human biomonitoring studies. To identify intracellular and extracellular miRNAs responses to silica-particle exposure in human THP-1 derived macrophages, differentiated THP-1 derived macrophages were exposed to 0-300 µg/mL crystalline silica particles for 24 h. Cytotoxicity was assessed

documents.title: Development of a Knowledge Map for Managing Symptoms of Graft-Versus-Host Disease in Patients Undergoing Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation.
documents.abstract: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) remains a critical complication affecting patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), with multifaceted symptoms requiring systematic management. Current clinical practices lack structured tools to guide nurses in addressing GVHD-related symptoms across diverse organ systems. This review aims to synthesize evidence on GVHD symptom management to construct a knowledge graph, enhancing nursing interventions and improving patient outcomes.

documents.title: Cutibacterium acnes induces T-cell extracellular traps with distinct proteome programs.
documents.abstract: Cutibacterium acnes is a common skin commensal associated with acne pathogenesis. In this study, we investigated whether acne-associated (denoted as CA) (HL043PA1) and healthy skin-associated (denoted as CH) (HL110PA3) C acnes strains differentially induce extracellular traps (ETs) in human neutrophils (neutrophil ETs) and T helper 17 cells (T-cell ETs [TETs]) and defined their proteomic and functional properties. Both strains triggered rapid ET release from neutrophils and T helper 17 cells. However, whereas neutrophil ETs displayed a conserved proteomic profile regardless of the strain, TETs

documents.title: Reactive astrocyte subpopulations with high Gfap and C4b expression in different Alzheimer's disease mouse models: Single-cell nuclear transcriptome analysis.
documents.abstract: Understanding the cellular landscape underlying the heterogeneity of Alzheimer’s disease and the cell type-specific molecular perturbations is essential for identifying novel, targeted therapeutic strategies. However, previous bulk transcriptomic studies have failed to capture the unique contributions of individual cell populations to the early pathogenesis of the disease, and the functional diversity of key cell types in driving Alzheimer’s disease progression remains insufficiently characterized. In this study, we examined transcriptional changes in hippocampal tissue during early Alzheimer’

documents.title: Reframing QSP: AI-Driven Multi-Modal Data as a New Measurement Layer.
documents.abstract: Quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) provides a mechanistic framework for integrating biological and pharmacological knowledge in drug development. Simultaneously, advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in multi-modal data analysis, are transforming how biological information is derived. I argue that AI should not be viewed as a data integration tool, but as a new layer of quantitative measurement generation. This reframing positions QSP as a foundational model of biology, used here in a conceptual rather than technical sense, and AI as a source of quantitative inputs.

documents.title: PDBe-SIFTS: An open-source tool for Structure Integration with Function, Taxonomy, and Sequences, featuring improved alignment, scoring scheme, and accelerated search.
documents.abstract: Structure integration with function, taxonomy and sequences (SIFTS) provides residue-level mappings between UniProt Knowledgebase sequences and Protein Data Bank structures and has historically been generated through internal Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe) pipelines. Here, PDBe-SIFTS is presented as a fully open-source, locally deployable implementation of this mapping framework. The pipeline combines fast, scalable sequence search using MMseqs2, an improved bounded scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and residue-level mapping refinement based on backbone connectivity. PDBe-SIFT
documents.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society

documents.title: EXPERT: A practical and forward-looking guide to capturing protein expression and purification metadata to develop machine learning models.
documents.abstract: As machine learning (ML) becomes increasingly important in protein engineering, synthetic biology, and bioprocess optimization, the lack of consistent, complete, and standardized experimental reporting remains a major barrier to building effective models. EXPERT (EXpression and Purification Experimental Reporting Template) defines a structured framework for capturing protein expression and purification data across the community, to increase reproducibility across laboratories and support downstream ML applications. We propose here the essential data that should be recorded during expression an

documents.title: Single-cell chromatin accessibility atlas decodes bone development, diseases, and regeneration.
documents.abstract: Bone development, homeostasis, and regeneration are governed by complex, dynamic gene regulatory programs, and these processes are disrupted in numerous skeletal diseases. The epigenetic landscape-particularly chromatin accessibility-dictates transcription factor binding and gene expression, which fundamentally shape bone cell fate and function. In recent years, single-cell chromatin accessibility technologies, most notably single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), have revolutionized bone epigenome research and enabled single-cell resolution dissect

documents.title: Comparative Transcriptomic and Physiological Profiling Reveals Species-Associated Differences Across Five Duckweed Species.
documents.abstract: Duckweeds (Lemnaceae) are fast-growing aquatic monocots with potential for biomass production and phytoremediation, but baseline molecular and physiological differences among species remain poorly characterized. We assembled de novo transcriptomes of five duckweed species, Lemna minor, Lemna japonica, Lemna gibba, Landoltia punctata, and Lemna aequinoctialis, grown on basal Murashige and Skoog (MS) medium (three biological replicates per species), and evaluated for completeness with Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs (BUSCO) against Viridiplantae, Embryophyta, and Liliopsida referenc

documents.title: A Traditional Chinese Medicine Knowledge Graph for Hypertension With Emotional Comorbidity: Development and Blinded Question-Answering Evaluation.
documents.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) literature on hypertension with anxiety, depression, or insomnia contains descriptions of syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs. A focused knowledge graph can organize these associations and their sources, but its contribution to generated answers requires separate evaluation.

documents.title: Integration of genotyping by sequencing and machine learning for genome-wide identification of informative markers for body weight in broiler chickens.
documents.abstract: Identifying associations between single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and economically important traits is fundamental to modern poultry breeding programs. However, genome-wide studies based on commercial high-density SNP arrays are often prohibitively expensive, particularly for large populations and in resource-limited settings. Therefore, this study employed a cost-effective genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) approach combined with two ensemble machine learning algorithms, Random Forest (RF) and Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), to identify informative markers of body weight (BW) at hatch, 3 w

documents.title: Dingent: A Configurable Agent Framework for Biological Database Retrieval and Integration.
documents.abstract: Natural-language retrieval across biological databases requires resource-specific tools, model instructions, and coordinated query steps. We present Dingent, an open-source agent framework that composes resource-specific tools into explicit multistep retrieval paths, integrating data-access plugins, configurable assistants, directed workflows, and web interfaces. Within this framework, developers expose resource functions as tools, administrators configure assistants and workflows, and users query the resulting application in natural language. We compared Dingent with a single-assistant tool-c

documents.title: PhageLysData: an evidence-aware and AI-ready dataset of phage lytic enzymes and depolymerases.
documents.abstract: Bacteriophage lytic enzymes and depolymerases are relevant to phage biology, antimicrobial development, and protein engineering, but their sequence and annotation data remain dispersed across general databases, specialized resources, genome-centred collections, and prediction-oriented datasets. We present PhageLysData, an evidence-aware and AI-ready resource constructed through reproducible multisource integration, provenance tracking, and exact-sequence consolidation. The release integrates 807,366 source observations from seven primary resources into 759,105 unique exact-sequence entities, c

documents.title: Advancing FAIR data management through AI-assisted curation of morphological data matrices.
documents.abstract: Curation of biological and paleontological datasets is a labor-intensive process that requires standardization and validation to ensure data integrity. In particular, manual curation of datasets is prone to human errors such as typographical errors, inconsistent formatting, and incomplete metadata, which hinder reproducibility and compliance with Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reusability (FAIR) principles. Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers a transformative solution for enhancing research efficiency by automating data validation, improving accuracy, and streamlining curati

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Multifaceted Toolkit for Antibacterial Drug Discovery against Resistance.
documents.abstract: How artificial intelligence (AI) can be rationally applied to antibacterial drug discovery and development to overcome antimicrobial resistance (AMR) remains insufficiently defined, particularly across different resistance mechanisms and translational stages. The global emergence and dissemination of AMR are compromising conventional antibacterial therapies, while slow antibiotic discovery, limited target diversity, and reliance on single-mechanism drug design further increase the risk of inadequate treatment options.
